stories.headline: Diwali gifts up to ₹15,000 tax-free; cash bonus is taxable salary
points: Under the Income-tax Act 2025, employer gifts and vouchers have nil taxable value if combined under ₹15,000 in a tax year.
Cash or cash-convertible gifts like gift cheques are fully taxable, and a cash bonus is added to salary income.
Form 130 replaces Form 16 as the salary TDS certificate from tax year 2026-27 onwards.
stories.why_it_matters: Perquisite valuation, salary TDS and the new Form 130 are core payroll and tax-compliance topics for CA and CMA students.
stories.source_title: Received Diwali bonus or cash from your employer? Know ₹15,000 exemption limit and when income tax applies | Explained
check_notes: Headline says gifts 'up to ₹15,000' are tax-free, but the source says the combined value must be 'below ₹15,000'. That is a small difference in wording at the exact threshold.

The headline's 'Diwali gifts up to ₹15,000' doesn't say the limit covers all qualifying gifts combined over the whole tax year and isn't limited to Diwali. Point 1 does say the limit is combined per tax year, so this is a wording issue only.

The Form 130 point closely paraphrases the source sentence ('Form 130 replaces Form 16 for salary TDS certificates from tax year 2026-27 onwards') but doesn't copy it word for word. Consider rewording it further.

stories.headline: ITAT Mumbai upholds penalty on bogus purchases despite 12.5% cut
points: ITAT Mumbai dismissed an appeal against a ₹1,84,771 penalty under Section 271(1)(c) for AY 2009-10.
The AO had added ₹43,48,834 of alleged hawala purchases; the Tribunal earlier cut the addition to 12.5% as profit element.
The Tribunal held that the cut did not make the penalty invalid, as the purchases were established as bogus on record.
stories.why_it_matters: Shows how penalty for concealment can stand even when a quantum addition is reduced, a key point in tax litigation and assessments.
stories.source_title: Income Tax | Penalty on Bogus Purchases Upheld Despite Restriction of Addition to 12.5% Profit Element: ITAT Mumbai
check_notes: Headline wording '12.5% cut' is ambiguous: it could be read as the addition being reduced by 12.5%, when the Tribunal actually restricted it to 12.5% of the bogus purchases. The second point states this correctly, so this is a wording issue only.

stories.headline: ITAT Jaipur allows full leave encashment exemption to SBI retiree
points: CPC had capped the exemption at ₹3 lakh and added ₹6,53,763 to the SBI retiree's income for AY 2020-21.
The Tribunal condoned a 992-day delay, citing the counsel's lapse, on payment of ₹10,000 to the PM's National Relief Fund.
It treated the ₹25 lakh limit as remedial, so the full ₹9,53,763 was exempt and the addition was ordered deleted.
stories.why_it_matters: Shows how Section 10(10AA) limits, delay condonation and the remedial reading of notifications can affect assessments and appeals.
stories.source_title: Income Tax | Remedial Leave Encashment Revision Supports Full Exemption for SBI Retiree: ITAT Jaipur
